integration_instruction: Append these unique items by ID to canonical emergence.json; retain existing required_prompts/items/histories unchanged, then regenerate centrally. This is a lane fragment, not the canonical register.

items.title: Source-processing review and current source policy are independent gates
items.origin: Events roadmap lane build at f749627f9f7456ddcc5744f22374c57f8c5e64be
items.observation: A whole-matter grant and an explicit review of incoming text do not establish current object quarantine, retention or processing/egress permission. Revocation between preview or claim and consumption must still deny; missing policy cannot default to a local test adapter.
items.product_implication: Keep explicit receipt/revision review separate from factual attestation and action authority. Wire current identity/vault/provider source policy transactionally before agency processing; make denial visible rather than weakening checks. Extra review/policy checks add integration and operator burden, but a permissive default would leak data.

history.by: Devin / events engineering lane (not owner sign-off)
history.reason: Existing task refinement: mandatory fail-closed policy callback implemented and negatively tested; production adapter/native integration remains unaccepted, not a new required task.

items.title: Uncertain event processing must retain disposition without automatic provider replay
items.origin: Events roadmap lane build at f749627f9f7456ddcc5744f22374c57f8c5e64be
items.observation: A durable claim may outlive cancellation, worker revocation, lease expiry or a failed result-storage transaction. A repeated processing request after such a failure could duplicate a paid or non-recallable call even though no reviewable result was persisted.
items.product_implication: Claim and run-marker persistence precede one explicit call. Keep original bounded late output as inert trace where storage succeeds; do not publish stale/cancelled results, resume on restart or claim an external request was recalled. Storage failure can still prevent retaining raw output; operator inspection is preferable to invented success.

history.by: Devin / events engineering lane (not owner sign-off)
history.reason: Existing task refinement: explicit attempt lifecycle, retained safe failure codes and no automatic re-execution implemented; paid/live provider and production crash/recovery acceptance stay open.

items.title: Conservative replan reuse must retain explicit clocks and approval revisions
items.origin: Events roadmap lane build at f749627f9f7456ddcc5744f22374c57f8c5e64be
items.observation: Revision-only case changes can leave planning inputs unchanged, but action approvals depend on the exact revision and expiry. Reusing a result while omitting approval revision or as-of clock could revive expired or invalid authority.
items.product_implication: Use detached bounded exact-input/clock caching with revision-only reuse only when approvals are absent, and full ENDSTATE fallback for all other changes. This gives a narrowly testable optimization without inventing a broad partial-graph algorithm; conservative fallback may offer little speedup on changing cases.

history.by: Devin / events engineering lane (not owner sign-off)
history.reason: Existing task refinement: conservative cache and exact full-response parity tested. General incremental-graph performance/production throughput remains an explicit limitation, not a passed gate.

items.title: A bounded retry ceiling needs an explicit operator recovery policy
items.origin: Events roadmap lane build at f749627f9f7456ddcc5744f22374c57f8c5e64be
items.observation: Three retained explicit attempts prevent silent retry loops, but exhausting that ceiling leaves no in-place reset. An operator may need to distinguish an invalid source or withdrawn consent from an infrastructure incident without erasing history or forging a new success.
items.product_implication: Evaluate a separately reviewed recovery workflow that preserves source, failure and billing/permission history, rather than adding unlimited resets or automatic retries. It could reduce operator friction, but may undermine budgets or encourage duplicate paid calls if policy is loose.

history.by: Devin / events engineering lane (not owner sign-off)
history.reason: Candidate recovery UX/policy requires owner/provider-budget decisions and observed operator need. Current bounded attempts remain; no reset bypass or extra required scope implemented.

items.title: Pre-commit local stage metrics are not combined provider or human latency evidence
items.origin: Events roadmap lane build at f749627f9f7456ddcc5744f22374c57f8c5e64be
items.observation: Local ingestion/processor/review timers can be retained on an atomic review record, but in-transaction durations stop before durability commit. Deterministic clocks in fixtures can verify instrumentation without measuring real inference or human review; mixed fixture and wall clocks yield incomparable waiting totals.
items.product_implication: Label metric scope, keep unknown historical durations null and retain the limitation instead of treating a fast scripted fixture as product performance. Integrated monotonic/UTC instrumentation and separately authorized real-provider/operator measurements are still needed.

history.by: Devin / events engineering lane (not owner sign-off)
history.reason: Existing task refinement: local instrumentation and honest fictional timings retained; combined durability/provider/human and production latency gates remain open.
